about: SolidCraft commands (for run_commands) and example features as stored in a design (for write_document and edit_document add). Built by scripts/feature-catalog.mjs.

commands.label: Create Sketch
commands.params: plane: XY|XZ|YZ (sketch x, y along world +X, +Y on XY; +X, -Z on XZ; +Y, +Z on YZ) | construction plane name or id | {origin?: [x,y,z] numbers in mm, default [0,0,0] (not an expression), x_dir, y_dir} (in world coordinates unless frame says otherwise; a named plane is the active component's own) | {face: [world x,y,z], body?: exact world body, index?: face index, path?: complete occurrence ids, fixed?: bool}; new face attachments require a unique certified source (a flat face of a sheet metal body attaches to its panel instead, in the flat pattern's coordinates), fixed:true explicitly freezes the selected plane; offset?: expr, flip?: bool | "x" | "y" (not on a face: sketch the plane from its other side, so the normal and the default extrude direction are reversed; a half turn about the plane's own x or y axis, true picks the one keeping the sketch's y axis upward; offset still moves along the unflipped normal), frame?: world (default) | component (which coordinates an explicit plane is in; the reply's `frame` says which, with a `note` when the active component is moved or turned), project_edges?: bool, activate_part?: bool (default false; on a face of a body of another component than the active one: activate that component at the picked placement first, as component.activate would, and make the sketch there; it stays active afterwards and the reply's `activated` names it), name?

commands.label: Edit Sketch
commands.params: sketch: id or name; restore_marker?: nonnegative timeline position, null (end) or false. A position or null: temporarily roll to this sketch and restore that position on Finish or Cancel; Finish groups the edit into one Undo step. Omitted: the same with the current position when features come after the sketch, so they rebuild once at Finish rather than after every sketch command. false: leave the timeline in place (later features rebuild after every sketch command)

commands.label: Finish Sketch
commands.params: restore_marker?: bool (default true); false transfers the temporary marker directly to another editor without rebuilding the intervening timeline

commands.label: Cancel Sketch
commands.params: Leaves the sketch without keeping what changed since it was created or opened for editing: the design goes back to how it was then (a new sketch is removed), as one step that Undo brings back. Refused when the undo history no longer leads back to that point (use Undo instead). restore_marker?: bool (default true); false transfers the temporary marker to another editor

commands.label: Line
commands.params: points: [[x,y] | "l1.end" | {at, ref}…] (x and y each a number or an expression over the design's parameters, "W / 2": such a point is fixed where it comes to and follows the parameters, while text naming no parameter, such as "5", is just that number, in the design's length unit (a JSON number is mm), and does not itself fix the point; likewise wherever a point argument also takes a point id), closed?: bool, construction?: bool, ids?: [..], infer?: bool (add horizontal/vertical); connect?: bool (default true: a new point landing exactly on an existing point, the origin too, is made coincident with it). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

commands.label: Draw Dimensioned Sketch Geometry

Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

commands.label: Sketch Dimension
commands.params: entities: [refs] (a line midpoint is "mid:line_id"; a model edge or vertex, {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, is projected into the sketch first and measured there: a point against the projected edge measures the distance to it), type?: auto|distance|horizontal|distance_x|vertical|distance_y|length|radius|diameter|major|minor|angle, value?: number or expression (default: current; a bare number is in the design's units, e.g. 2 means 2 in in an inch design; give a unit such as "50 mm" to override), or `name = expression` (e.g. "width = 40"; also `#name = expression`), which adds the user parameter `name` with that expression and dimensions with `name` (refused when the name is taken or reserved; the reply's `defined` names it); text_at?: [x, y]. Two points or a line off the axes: with auto, text_at across from them (between the perpendiculars through them, or a tenth of their distance past) is the distance between them; pulled further past an end, up or down from it horizontal, sideways vertical. Two midpoints: placing text above or below their bounding box measures horizontally, beside it vertically, anywhere else (inside it or past its corners) the distance between them. Two lines: the angle between them (acute, or 180° − it when the value is nearer that) unless text_at picks a sector. A line and a circle or arc: the distance from the line to its edge (the gap, or how far the edge reaches past a line that cuts it; 0 is tangent); dimension the centre point for the distance to the centre. A point and a circle or arc: the distance from the point to its edge (or how far within it a point inside lies). Two circles or arcs: the gap between their edges (or how far they overlap when they cross, or the narrowest gap between them when one lies inside the other), or the centre-to-centre distance when they are the two caps of a slot. An ellipse: a half-axis, the distance from the centre to an axis end (major or minor; with auto, text_at pulled across the major axis gives the major half-axis, pulled out past an end of it the minor one, the minor without text_at; previous_axis?: major|minor, the half-axis an earlier placement chose, kept while text_at is near the boundary between them; the reply's axis names the one chosen; with auto, when a driving dimension already holds one half-axis (or its whole axis), the other one, wherever text_at is; without its major axis line the major half-axis goes to the ellipse's own major end, without its minor axis line the minor half-axis is the minor radius); any other type, radius among them, the minor radius; an ellipse's axis line with auto: its length, the whole axis, wherever text_at is; half_axes?: bool (default true; false: with auto, the minor radius wherever text_at is, as before half-axes, which the Dimension tool sends with Draw ellipses with their axes off). An arc and one of its end points: the arc's length (type arc_length does it from the arc alone). A dimension the sketch already determines is refused (naming what determines it); if_redundant?: "driven" places it as a driven (reference) dimension instead. scale_sketch?: bool (the dimension tool sends the Sketch preference, on by default): when this is the sketch's first length dimension and nothing in the sketch fixes a size (no other driving length dimension, nothing fixed or projected), the whole sketch scales to the value instead of distorting: about the origin when the drawing is tied to it (joined to the origin, or constrained to a sketch axis), otherwise about the middle of the drawing, so it stays where it was drawn (#11043); scale_about_origin?: bool (default false; the dimension tool sends the Sketch preference) scales about the origin always, as before #11043. Returns measured in unit (mm or deg), and scaled: the factor when the sketch was scaled

commands.label: Horizontal/Vertical
commands.params: line: id | points: [a, b] (point ids or {midpoint: line_id}; accepted midpoints reuse or create a point with a Midpoint constraint); mode?: horizontal|vertical

commands.label: Coincident
commands.params: a, b: points (or a line's middle as {midpoint: line}, which becomes a point tied there), a point and a curve or sketch axis (x / y: the sketch's own axes, unless a curve has that id; an axis becomes a linked construction line on it, reported in created), or two distinct lines (joins their closest endpoints), or two circles/arcs (the second lies on the first: concentric and equal, `constraints` lists both); any of them may be a model edge {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or vertex {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, projected into the sketch first (reported in created)

commands.label: Tangent
commands.params: a, b: curves or sketch axes (x / y: the sketch's own axes, unless a curve has that id; an axis becomes a linked construction line on it, reported in created), or the end point of a line or an arc: that end then lies on the other curve (or on the other end point), and its curve is tangent there, in one step (`constraints` lists both); any of them may be a model edge {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or vertex {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, projected into the sketch first (reported in created)

commands.label: Equal
commands.params: a, b: lines or circles/arcs; or curves: [2 to 200 lines or circles/arcs], each made equal to the first, in one step; any of them may be a model edge {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or vertex {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, projected into the sketch first (reported in created)

commands.label: Parallel
commands.params: a, b: lines or sketch axes (x / y: the sketch's own axes, unless a curve has that id; an axis becomes a linked construction line on it, reported in created); any of them may be a model edge {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or vertex {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, projected into the sketch first (reported in created)

commands.label: Perpendicular
commands.params: a, b: lines or sketch axes (x / y: the sketch's own axes, unless a curve has that id; an axis becomes a linked construction line on it, reported in created); any of them may be a model edge {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or vertex {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, projected into the sketch first (reported in created)

commands.label: Fix/Unfix
commands.params: entity: point or curve | entities: [points and curves]; fixed?: bool (default: fix them all unless all are fixed, then unfix); unfixing a point placed by parameter expressions (`sketch.inspect` shows them as its `fixed_by`) frees it where they come to now, as plain numbers

commands.label: MidPoint
commands.params: point, line | a, b in pick order: a point and a line (either way round), or two lines whose midpoints meet (the first stays, the second moves); any of them may be a model edge {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or vertex {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, projected into the sketch first (reported in created)

commands.label: Concentric
commands.params: a, b: two circles/arcs, or a circle/arc and a sketch point (including origin), in either order; the point and the curve's centre become coincident; any of them may be a model edge {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or vertex {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, projected into the sketch first (reported in created)

commands.label: Collinear
commands.params: a, b: lines or sketch axes (x / y: the sketch's own axes, unless a curve has that id; an axis becomes a linked construction line on it, reported in created); any of them may be a model edge {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or vertex {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, projected into the sketch first (reported in created)

commands.label: Symmetry
commands.params: a, b: two points or two curves (lines mirror their ends, circles/arcs their centres); line: symmetry line id, or x / y for the sketch's own axes (a curve with that id wins; an axis becomes a linked construction line on it, reported in created); or point (or a point id as line, "origin" too): symmetric about that point, each pair joined by a construction line it is the midpoint of; any of them may be a model edge {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or vertex {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, projected into the sketch first (reported in created)

commands.label: Normal/Construction
commands.params: curves: [ids], value?: bool (default: construction unless all of them already are)

commands.label: Delete Sketch Entities
commands.params: entities: [curve, point or constraint ids]

commands.label: Drag Sketch Point
commands.params: point: ref, to: [x,y]

commands.label: Move Sketch Points
commands.params: moves: [{point: ref | near: [x,y], to: [x,y]}] (each point to its own target; `near`: the sketch point closest to it, refused when none lies within `tolerance` or two are as close), tolerance?: mm (default 0.1); sketch? → moved: [{point, to, at, reached}] (`at`: where it ended up after the one solve; `reached`: whether that is `to`); a point placed by parameter expressions is refused, naming them (unfix it with sketch.constraint.fix first)

commands.label: Drag Sketch Geometry
commands.params: entity: point or curve, from: [x,y] where it was grabbed, to: [x,y], live?: bool: points and the material point grabbed on a line move toward `to` within the design constraints. When exact placement is impossible, bounded feasible steps minimize cursor distance. Splines slide by to - from; a circle or arc grabbed on its edge takes the radius to `to`. `with?`: [point or curve ids] moves the rest of a selection with the entity as one translation (circles keep their radii). Long moves retain the solution branch; arcs cannot sweep through their starts. Returns `reached`: progress projected onto the requested move (0..1), `at`: the grabbed position for the next frame, and `retry`: budget-limited progress can continue in another frame. `live: true` shares a work budget across held-solve decomposition and cursor correction; ordinary recovery and the final model evaluation retain their existing limits, not a wall-clock deadline. Later features stay stale until `sketch.drag_end`; `dof` stays from before the drag

commands.label: End Sketch Drag
commands.params: constraint?: {command: a sketch.constraint.* id, params}: ends a drag made of `sketch.drag` `live: true` frames: adds the constraint it let go on (not kept if it over-constrains the sketch), then evaluates the whole model once; returns the constraint's result and the sketch's solved state and degrees of freedom

commands.params: center: slot centre, end: one arc centre, width; returns centre_line and middle. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

commands.params: center, start: centre arc start, end: direction of the centre arc end (counter-clockwise) or sweep: degrees (0 < sweep < 360), width; returns centre_arc and middle. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

commands.label: Ellipse
commands.params: center, major: end of the major axis [x,y] (a coordinate of either may be an expression over the design's parameters: the point follows them), minor: a point the ellipse passes through on the minor side [x,y] | minor_radius: number or expression (an expression naming a parameter is a dimension driven by it). Also adds its major and minor axes as construction lines through the centre (their ends: the major end and the point opposite it, and the two ends of the minor axis on the ellipse), held by midpoint, perpendicular and point-on-curve constraints, so a half-axis is the distance from the centre to an axis end and an axis line's length is a full axis; axes?: bool (default true; false: the ellipse alone, as the Ellipse tool draws it with Draw ellipses with their axes off). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

commands.label: Fit Point Spline
commands.params: points: [[x,y] or point refs…] (2…500): the spline passes through them; each fit point has an editable tangent handle whose direction and length control curvature, periodic?: boolean (default false); periodic cubic fit closes smoothly through at least 3 distinct samples. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

commands.label: Control Point Spline
commands.params: points: control points (2…500), cubic. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

commands.label: Control Point Spline (Degree 5)
commands.params: points: control points (2…500), degree 5. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

commands.label: Add Spline Point
commands.params: curve: fit point spline id, at: [x,y]: a fit point is inserted where the curve passes nearest to it, between its neighbours (the curve still runs through it and all its old points; constraints on them stay); end?: start|end: `at` becomes the spline's new first or last point instead, and the curve runs on to it (refused when that end is joined to other geometry). Control point splines take no new points yet. Returns point: the new point's id

commands.label: Remove Spline Point
commands.params: curve: spline id, point: one of its points (a point id, or the curve's start or end such as s1.end): the spline runs through (or over) its other points only, and the point goes with the constraints on it unless another curve uses it. Fit point, control point and closed splines. Refused for a closed spline's closing point, for an end joined to other geometry or held by a constraint, when fewer than 2 points would be left (3 on a closed spline), and for a projected, offset or patterned spline. Returns curve, point: the point's id, deleted: whether the point went too

commands.label: Add Tangent Handles
commands.params: curve: fit point spline id: gives it a tangent handle at each fit point (a free point joined to it by a construction line) where the curve already runs, so its shape does not change until a handle is moved; moving a fit point moves the handles nobody has turned with it. In the app a selected spline shows its handles and the first drag of one adds them. Refused for a spline that has handles already, a control point, projected, offset, patterned or equation spline. Returns curve, handles: the handle point ids in fit point order

commands.label: Reset Tangent Handles
commands.params: curve: fit point spline id: removes its tangent handles (the handle points, their construction lines and the constraints on them), so the curve runs through its fit points as if the handles had never been moved; selected, it shows them again where they start. Refused for a spline without tangent handles. Returns curve, removed: the removed handle point ids in fit point order

commands.label: Reverse Spline Direction
commands.params: curve: spline id (fit point, control point or closed): its last point becomes its first and the curve runs the other way along the same path; its points and the constraints on them stay. Refused for a projected spline and for one an offset uses or makes. Returns curve

commands.label: Divide Curve
commands.params: curve: id | curves: [ids] (each divided on its own); segments: whole number from 2 to 500. Places points that divide each curve into `segments` pieces of equal length along it (arc length): segments − 1 points on an open curve (line, arc, spline, conic), `segments` points on a closed one (a circle from its point on sketch +X, an ellipse from its major-axis end, a closed spline from its first point). Each point is constrained to its share of the curve's length, so it stays on the curve and keeps equal spacing as the curve changes; the curve is not changed. Infinite lines are refused. Returns points: [ids], per curve in order, and constraints: [ids]. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

commands.label: Equation Curve
commands.params: x: x(t), y: y(t): formulas of t in the design's expression language and parameters ("r * (cos(t) + t * sin(t))"); or explicit: true and y: f(x) alone (no x); start, end: the range of t (or of x): a number or an expression ("2 * pi", "360 deg" is 2·pi, a length is in the design's unit); tolerance?: mm (default 0.01): how far the curve may stray from the formulas (0.0001 to 10); construction?: bool; variable_unit?: "number" (default) or "range". The variable is a plain number: sin(t) reads it in radians; a result without a unit is in the design's length unit. With variable_unit "range" it is a length, so a ^ 2 / (4 * t) is a length when a is one: start and end must both be lengths, or one a length and the other a plain number, which is then in the design's unit. Makes a fit point spline through fixed points, as many as the tolerance needs (up to 500), closed smoothly when it ends where it starts; the points are placed again from the formulas whenever the parameters change. Returns curve, points (how many), closed, deviation (mm). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

commands.label: Flange
commands.params: base: sketch + profiles? (rule?, flip?) | contour: sketch + curves (open chain of lines and tangent arcs) + distance (rule?, flip?, reverse?) | edge: edges: [[x,y,z] on top/bottom edges, or {point: [x,y,z], angle?, height?, segments?} for an edge with its own angle and height, or split into 1…64 segments [{from, to, angle?, height?, flip?}] that tile the stretch the sheet still has there (from, to are fractions 0…1 of it, first from 0, last to 1; consecutive segments that match make one bend)] + height (along the flange, to its far edge), angle? (default 90 deg), radius? (default: rule), height_from?: outer|inner|tangent (where the height is measured from: the outer virtual sharp (default), the inner virtual sharp, or past 90 deg the line square to the flange touching the bend's outside (tangent; up to 90 deg the outer sharp)), position?: inside|outside|middle|material_outside|tangent (where the bend starts: the outer virtual sharp on the edge (default), the bend starting at the edge (bend_outside is the same), half way, the inner virtual sharp on the edge, or the bend's outer face tangent to the edge's face (below 90 deg the bend's end on that face)), flip?, body?, corner_relief_shape?: notch|round|rectangular|tear and corner_relief? (size across): the relief at the corners these flanges make (default: the rule's); then?: [{angle?, height, flip?}] further bends (at most 16), each a flange on the far edge of the one before, flip: true turns that bend the other way (edge only); type?: base|edge|contour (default from the inputs); name?, body_name? (the new body). Thickness, K-factor and bend radius come from the rule (sheet.manage_rules); passing them here is refused, and so is the corner relief on a base or contour flange

commands.label: Path Flange
commands.params: edge: [x,y,z] on a top or bottom edge of the sheet; sketch + curves: an open chain of sketch lines drawn on a plane across that edge, from the edge out (each line one flange as long as the line, to the outer face from the virtual sharp; each corner one bend, turning the way the lines turn); radius? (default: rule); body?. One feature, one body

(the outline: closed profiles of a sketch on a face of the sheet; holes only inside them, out of their inner loops) - a perforation field over the whole flat sheet or inside the outline: holes in the flat pattern (perforations), the DXF (layer PERFORATION) and the measured volume, not cut into the B-rep (#732)

commands.label: Hem

commands.label: Fold

(default: rule); position?: centerline|start|end|mould (where the line sits in the bend, default centerline); fixed?: [x,y,z] on the side that stays (default: the larger side); flip? (fold the other way); body?

commands.label: Unfold
commands.params: body? (default: the last sheet body) — all bends

commands.label: Refold
commands.params: body? (default: the last unfolded sheet)

commands.label: Convert to Sheet Metal
commands.params: body; face: [x,y,z] on its large flat face (a plate of even thickness; recesses in one face up to half the thickness deep, such as an engraved label, become pockets of the sheet), or that face's name from model.faces; rule?; bends?: [[x,y,z] on sharp edges] (a solid or a shelled body: `face` is the fixed face and the flat faces reached from it across these edges become the sheet; a shell keeps its thickness, a solid takes the rule's inward; edges between two of those faces that are no bends are cut open with the rule's gap; a point in the middle of a chamfer between two faces, or on a bend modelled with its radius (a cylinder between two flat faces tangent to it, either skin), makes it one bend of the rule's radius at their virtual sharp; the faces' holes become cut-outs and their engravings, up to half the thickness deep, pockets)

commands.label: Sheet Metal Rules
commands.params: name (new or existing); thickness?, k_factor?, bend_radius?, relief_width?, relief_depth?, corner_relief?, hem_gap?, gap? (expressions; `Thickness` is the rule's; gap: between flanges that meet at a corner, whose ends are closed toward each other at any angle); corner_relief_shape?: notch|round|rectangular|tear (what is cut where two bends meet at a corner of the base: round and rectangular a relief `corner_relief` across; tear none, each bend's end is cut straight from the corner to its flange's end; default notch); angle_display?: bend|included (how the DXF bend notes read the bend angles: the bend angle, default, or the included angle left between the bend's sides, 180° less it; the bend table gives both, and a flange's `angle` is always the bend angle); active?: bool; delete?: bool

commands.label: List Sheet Metal Rules
commands.params: → rules with their expressions and values, and the active one

commands.label: Create Flat Pattern
commands.params: body? → flat size, outline loops and cut-outs (flat coordinates, as point lists), cutout_shapes (the same cut-outs exactly, in the same order: {circle: {center, radius}} for a round hole, else {segments: [{line: [a, b]} | {arc: {center, radius, start_deg, sweep_deg}} | {polyline: [...]}]}), pockets (with their own cutout_shapes), bend lines and the bend table

commands.label: Export Flat Pattern as DXF
commands.params: body?, path?, curves?: exact|arcs (default exact: an ellipse as ELLIPSE, splines, text outlines and other Béziers as SPLINE; arcs: tangent arcs and lines within 0.001 mm, for machines that read only those), text?: cut|etch (default cut: letters that text cut through the sheet are cut contours on layer TEXT; etch: single contours on layer ETCH and the sheet keeps its material there; text machined to a depth is always on ETCH), bend_notes?: bool (default false: a note beside each bend line on layer BEND_NOTES, `B1 UP 90%%d R1`, its angle the included angle when the body's rule has angle_display: included), note_height?: mm (default 3), bend_lines?: bool (default true; false leaves BEND_UP and BEND_DOWN out, for a cutter that would cut them), layers?: roles|single (default roles, the layers below; single: every entity on layer 0), per_body?: bool (a file for every sheet body, `<path>-<body>.dxf`, or their DXF texts without a path → files: [{body, path | dxf, bends}]; not with `body`) → DXF (AutoCAD 2000, mm): layers OUTLINE (the outer contour), CUT (what is cut out inside it), TEXT or ETCH (letters), BEND_UP and BEND_DOWN (dashed centre lines), BEND_NOTES, POCKET_<BOTTOM|TOP|INTERNAL>_Z<from>_TO_<to>_MM (one per side and depth) and PERFORATION; inner contours come before the outline

commands.label: Export Bend Table
commands.params: body?, format?: csv|json (default csv), path? → bend table in mm and degrees, including rule and flat centre-line coordinates; angle_deg is the bend angle and included_angle_deg the angle left between the bend's sides (180° less it); a bend that cut-outs split has a row for each piece

commands.params: name (library or new rule; a new one starts from `from`, default ABS (1.5mm)); from?; material?; thickness?, nominal_radius?, clearance?, knife_edge?, reveal_height?, thickness_variation?, draft?, max_thickness?, min_thickness?, min_draft? (expressions; `Thickness` is the rule's); active?: bool (rule for bodies without one); delete?: bool (a design rule; a library rule goes back to the library values)

commands.params: → rules with their expressions and values, the active rule and the rules assigned to bodies

commands.label: Frame Member
commands.params: sketch: the frame sketch (id or name; 2D or 3D); lines?: [curve ids] (one member each; default: every straight line drawn in the sketch: not construction, not projected or otherwise linked, not of no length); profile: {kind: bar|round_bar|rect_tube|round_tube|angle|channel|i_beam, …its dimensions: each a number in the design's units or a length expression over its parameters ("tube_wall", "2 in"); a channel's flange_slope is an angle (a number of degrees)} (frame.profile.list gives each kind's dimensions and an example; dimensions left out take defaults from the profile's size) | {size: a standard steel size by name, such as "RSC 203x89", "PFC 200x90x30", "RSA 50x50x5", "SHS 100x100x5", "RHS 200x100x6.3" or "CHS 42.4x3.2" (frame.profile.list lists them), alone: it brings its dimensions} | profile_sketch: a sketch whose profile is the section, in its own x and y around its origin, with profiles?: picks as solid.extrude takes them (default: its material, nested loops alternating, so two circles make a tube); anchor?: origin|center|centroid|top_left|top|top_right|left|right|bottom_left|bottom|bottom_right (the profile point that sits on each line, default origin); locate?: [x,y] (the profile point that sits on each line, in mm from the profile's own origin: a bar's or an angle's bottom-left corner, a channel's web back at mid-height, the centre of other profiles; takes precedence over `anchor` and keeps the member attached at that point when the profile size changes); angle?: angle expr (the profile turned about the line; default 0: its y as near world up as the line allows, a vertical member's x along world X); mirror?: bool (the profile mirrored across its y axis); name?; body_name? Returns kinds: [{kind, label, required, optional, example}]: the built-in profiles, each SolidCraft's own parametric definition; and sizes: [{family, kind, standard, source, names, additional?}]: the standard steel sizes by name, each family with the published table its dimensions come from (frame.profile.properties with {profile: {size}} gives a size's dimensions and section)

commands.label: Insert Profile
commands.params: profile: {kind: bar|round_bar|rect_tube|round_tube|angle|channel|i_beam, …its dimensions: each a number in the design's units or a length expression over its parameters ("tube_wall", "2 in"); a channel's flange_slope is an angle (a number of degrees)} (frame.profile.list gives each kind's dimensions and an example; dimensions left out take defaults from the profile's size) | {size: a standard steel size by name, such as "RSC 203x89", "PFC 200x90x30", "RSA 50x50x5", "SHS 100x100x5", "RHS 200x100x6.3" or "CHS 42.4x3.2" (frame.profile.list lists them), alone: it brings its dimensions}; at?: [x,y] (sketch mm, default the origin); anchor?: origin|center|centroid|top_left|top|top_right|left|right|bottom_left|bottom|bottom_right (the profile point placed on `at`: its origin, the default and a built-in profile's centre, its bounding box's centre, its centroid, or a corner or edge middle of its bounding box); angle?: radians, counter-clockwise; fixed?: bool (default true: the curves are locked, so solving the sketch keeps the shape); sketch?: id|name (default: the sketch being edited). Returns the section as frame.profile.properties does. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

commands.label: End Cap
commands.params: faces: [{face:[x,y,z],body,index,path?}] planar end faces of frame members, picked in world mm (1–256); thickness: length in design units or a parameter expression; offset?: inset of the plate from the outside of the profile, a length; ratio?: the inset as a share of the thickness (give offset or ratio, not both; neither: the plate is flush with the outside of the profile); chamfer?: corner chamfer length along each edge from the corner (default 0; a rounded corner needs at least its rounding); direction?: outward|inward (default outward: past the end; inward: the member is cut back by the thickness and the cap takes its place). One separate body per face, named `<member> End Cap`; the plate is the profile's outer outline on a closed section (tube, pipe, bar), its outside on an open one (angle, channel, beam, slotted extrusion): the edges on the rectangle round the profile with their rounds and chamfers, inward stretches closed along the rectangle. Common name/body_names fields supported.

commands.label: Cycle Component Color
commands.params: component: id or name; saves the next identification colour and turns Component Colors on; shared by every instance, separate from appearances

commands.label: Hide Component History
commands.params: component: id or name; keeps the component's features in the design but leaves them out of the History bar (#10393)

commands.label: Show Component History
commands.params: component: id or name; puts a component's features back in the History bar after Hide Component History (#10393)

commands.label: New Component
commands.params: name?, parent?: component id or name (default: the active one); parent_path?: exact parent placement; activate?: bool (default true); grounded?: bool (default: true for the design's first part, false otherwise)

commands.label: Create Components from Bodies
commands.params: bodies: [names] → one new component per body, named after it

commands.label: Activate Component
commands.params: component: id or name (0 or "root" for the design); occurrence?, path?: exact placement used to author shared geometry

commands.label: Edit in Place
commands.params: component: id or name of a linked component; path?: its placement (occurrence ids, default its first) → in the app window: open the design it links in a tab of its own with the assembly drawn around it (component.finish_edit goes back); fails when it is not linked, the assembly has no file yet, something is open or running in it, or the file is missing, on a network location not allowed yet or open in another SolidCraft; asked during the agent's turn it opens once the turn ends (queued: true); elsewhere it only checks

commands.label: Finish Edit
commands.params: no parameters → in the app window: go back from the linked design edited in place to its assembly, which reads it again; fails while the design has unsaved changes (run file.save first) or something is open in it; asked during the agent's turn it finishes once the turn ends (queued: true); elsewhere nothing changes

commands.label: List Components
commands.params: compact?: bool (counts of bodies, features, sketches and construction planes instead of their names; occurrences leave out identity transforms; children as occurrence ids); bodies?: bool (with compact: body names, not their count)

commands.label: Component Physical Properties
commands.params: component?: id or name (default active); descendants?: bool (default true); about?: [x, y, z] (mm). Measures the first placement, or all placements for root, including pending moves; material-aware mass and center of mass in world coordinates; volume, density, mass, center of mass and inertia_g_mm2 (the inertia tensor about the body's center of mass, world axes, from its tessellation) only for closed, consistently oriented bodies; total.open_bodies_skipped counts open bodies excluded from volume/mass totals; total.first_moment_g_mm (mass × center of mass), inertia_g_mm2 about the total center of mass, principal_moments_g_mm2 (smallest first) and principal_axes (unit, right-handed); with about, total.inertia_about {point, inertia_g_mm2}

commands.label: Occurrence Physical Properties
commands.params: occurrence: id or name; path?: [occurrence ids] (required if nested under multiple instances); descendants?: bool (default true); about?: [x, y, z] (mm). Physical properties of this placement in world coordinates, including pending moves; volume, density, mass, center of mass and inertia_g_mm2 only for closed, consistently oriented bodies; total.open_bodies_skipped counts open bodies excluded from volume/mass totals; total inertia as in component.properties

commands.label: Rename Component
commands.params: component, name

commands.label: Delete Component
commands.params: component: deletes it, its subcomponents, occurrences and features

commands.label: Unlock Contents
commands.params: component: removes the rigid joints that hold its contents together (an imported assembly's rigid group), so its parts move and take joints one by one → joints (the ids removed)

commands.label: Move Bodies to Component
commands.params: bodies: [names], component; component_path?: its placement to place them by (default: its only one, else the active one; a component placed more than once gets them in every instance); from_path?: the placement of their component they move from (default: its only one, else its first, where its bodies have their own names)

commands.label: Paste Bodies
commands.params: bodies: [names, as the Browser shows them: a body seen in another placement of its component (`Cube (B:2)`) is copied from there]; component?: where the copies go (default: the active one); component_path?: its placement to place them by (default: its only one, else the active one; a component placed more than once gets them in every instance). Each copy stays where its body is in the world; the copies' names come back as `bodies`

commands.label: Paste from Another Design
commands.params: component?: where it goes (default: the active one); component_path?: its placement (default: the active one, else its only one). Pastes what was copied in another design, at the same world coordinates: its bodies as imported bodies (no history) in one Import feature, or its components as independent copies with their history, appearances, joints and motion (as `component.paste_new`); the user parameters they use come along, renamed `w_2` when taken. A component that uses what isn't in it (another body, sketch or parameter) is refused, saying what. Returns `bodies` and `feature`, or the pasted components' `paths`

commands.label: Move Sketches to Component
commands.params: sketches: [ids or names] (a number is an id; a string is an exact name, then an id), component; the sketches keep their own coordinates (component.move_features keeps them where they are in the world), except that a sketch on an exactly attached face stays where it is on the face

commands.label: Move Sketches to Their Parts
commands.params: sketches?: [ids or names] (default: every sketch in the design) → moved, stayed, sketches [{sketch, name, component, part}], kept [{sketch, name, code, reason}]. Each sketch whose plane is an exactly attached face of a part's body goes to that part, as component.move_sketches moves it, and stays where it is on the face; the others (on an origin, construction or fixed plane, on a body of the design itself, or already in their part) stay where they are. One undo step

commands.label: Move Features to Component
commands.params: features: [ids or names] (sketches too); component?: where they go (default: the active one) → moved, component, bodies. Ids, names and timeline order stay; the geometry stays where it is in the world; the bodies the features made move with them. Refused while the timeline is rolled back, for a component placed more than once, and for a move that would break a feature (nothing changes)

commands.label: Move to Component
commands.params: Moves placements, features and bodies into a component. occurrences?: [ids or paths], features?: [ids or names], bodies?: [names], component?: where they go (default: the active one), component_path?: its placement → component, occurrences, features, bodies (what moved). One undo step, all or nothing: placements move first (taking what they hold), then features (taking the bodies they made), then the bodies still elsewhere (a body transfer, which leaves its features behind)

commands.label: Paste (Instance)
commands.params: component (or occurrence): what to place again; path?: validates selected occurrence; parent?: component (default: the same parent); translate?: [x,y,z]; in_place?: bool (default false: the selected transform within the parent; true: where the selected placement is in the world, translate in world axes; a parent placed more than once is placed by parent_path?, else the active placement, and every instance gets the copy). Copies the selected effective transform, including pending moves

commands.label: Paste New
commands.params: component: independently copy its nested definition graph and history, materials and styles; occurrence?, path?: selected source placement; parent?: component the copy goes in (default: the source placement's; not the component or one inside it); in_place?, parent_path?: as occurrence.copy; translate?: [x,y,z]. Reassigned external bodies become base geometry; retained external links and omitted boundary joints are reported

commands.label: Move Occurrence
commands.params: occurrence; path?: exact placement; space?: local|world (default local); translate?: [x,y,z] (numbers or length expressions: an occurrence moved by expressions that name parameters keeps them and moves with them when the parameters change, along the axes the move was given in; other moves of it stay; a parameter they use can't be deleted, and a renamed one carries into them); axis?: [x,y,z], angle?: radians or "30 deg", origin?: [x,y,z]; to?: {position: [x,y,z], axis?: [x,y,z], angle?} or to_matrix?: [12 or 16 numbers] (absolute placement: where it goes in space, not a move; not with translate/axis/angle/origin/matrix); matrix?: [12 or 16 numbers] (instead of translate/axis/angle/origin: a rigid move as a row-major 3x4 rotation-and-translation or 4x4 matrix, flat or as rows; one that is a rotation only up to rounding is orthonormalised, a scale, shear or mirror is refused); tolerance?: largest accepted |RᵀR − I| (default 1e-9, at most 1e-3); capture?: bool (default true; false keeps it pending until Capture Position); move_grounded?: bool (default false: a grounded occurrence refuses; true moves it and it stays grounded). Replies {occurrence, transform, pending}; when joints hold it to something fixed and put it back, transform is where it is and the reply adds reverted: true and a warning naming the joint

commands.label: Drag Occurrence
commands.params: occurrence or path: exact placement; at: [x,y,z] world point on it; point: [x,y,z] where it goes. Moves the placement by point - at (with any chain of joints it is in that is joined to nothing grounded) and captures its position; other pending moves stay pending. Shared definitions move in all placements. Grounded parts and parts joints hold to something fixed are refused (joint.reach moves those)

commands.label: Align Occurrence
commands.params: occurrence?, occurrences?, path?, paths?: placements to move together; from | from_face | from_plane; to | to_face | to_plane; flip?: bool; capture?: bool (default true); move_grounded?: bool (default false). Moves only the chosen occurrence placements in world coordinates without changing shared component geometry; a placement inside a component placed more than once moves in every placement of it, and the reply's `shared` lists those paths

commands.label: Ground
commands.params: occurrence; grounded?: bool (default toggles)

commands.label: Move to Component
commands.params: occurrence; path?: exact placement; parent: component id or name (0 or "root" for the design); parent_path?: the parent's placement to place it by (default: its only one, else the active one; every instance of the parent gets it). The placement keeps its world position; a move that would break a feature is refused

commands.label: Capture Position
commands.params: keeps pending occurrence moves and saves every moving joint's values → captured, joints

commands.label: Revert Position

commands.label: Compare Bodies
commands.params: a, b: body names (default: the two selected bodies, or the design's only two), in world placement; tolerance?: mm (0.001 to 10, default 0.01): surfaces closer than this agree; spacing?: mm (default 0.5): the largest piece of a face sampled as one point, coarser for a body that would need more than max_points? (default 8 million, up to 50 million) samples; max_regions? (default 50); color?: true | {only_in_a?, only_in_b?: "#rrggbb"} (colours the faces that hold a region, red where only a has material and green where only b has: the faces mostly beyond the tolerance, else the one with the largest share; an undo step) → a, b: volume_mm3, area_mm2, center_of_mass, bbox; difference: b − a; deviation: a_to_b, b_to_a (max_mm, mean_mm, at, area_beyond_mm2); regions, largest first: side (only_in_a | only_in_b), volume_mm3, center and bbox (measured_by: "boolean": exact, the pieces of a − b or b − a there, measured as inspect.measure does; "not measured": the cut could not be made, so volume_mm3 and center are null and not_measured says why, never an estimate), area_mm2, max_deviation_mm, at, faces_a, faces_b (face indices, as model.faces lists them); identical; verdict; warnings (a body whose surface does not enclose what it measures, lines left out, a cut that could not be made). commands.label: Compare Picture

Validated finite light edit in one undo. Existing family caps and backend support apply; refusal is atomic. Names remain defaults.

commands.label: Remove Render Light
commands.params: name; id except add; settings?: full unsaved RenderSetup; expected_revision?:u64; set for set/add: kind directional/point/spot/area, intensity_ev, temperature_k, softness, azimuth_deg, elevation_deg, distance_mm, size_mm, aim_at, width_mm, height_mm, position_mm, direction, edge_u_mm, edge_v_mm, radiance, colour, reference_distance_mm, minimum_distance_mm. Validated finite light edit in one undo. Existing family caps and backend support apply; refusal is atomic. Names remain defaults.

commands.label: List Render Lights
commands.params: setup?: saved setup name OR settings?: complete RenderSetup snapshot; neither uses defaults. Returns {lights:[{id,kind,name,name_key,number,implicit,intensity,colour,...spatial fields}]}. IDs are kind:zero-based-source-slot, stable across numerical edits but not family changes/reordering/removal/rig replacement; point and spot share punctual slots. Includes implicit default/preset lights. GPU RGB radiance is factored as colour * intensity; area edges are full world-mm vectors. Read-only, no host, camera change, save, render, model evaluation or undo. See docs/render-settings.md.

commands.label: Layered Surface Aging
commands.params: Empty object. Read-only original Rust/patina/dust/grime/scratch/chip/fading presets and exact GPU aging contract. UI activation opens the shared Aging tab; edits remain a saved render draft, never engineering geometry or material-property mutation.

commands.label: Lens and Creative Effects
commands.params: Empty object. Read-only original photographic/creative filter defaults and constraints. UI activation opens shared Effects controls. Saved finishing and exact-master regrading preserve raw EXR bytes; no physical lens or branded-film calibration is implied.

commands.label: Save Clear Coat
commands.params: name; set?: numerical setup patch; body_index/body_name: exact render.scene identity; expected_revision; coat:{weight:0..1,roughness:0.045..1,ior:1..3}; replace?:false. Stores up to the existing 64 target bound as stable definition/feature/component/occurrence bindings for CPU/GPU. Even zero-weight coats require opaque targets. Same-target Glass refuses. One undo; no geometry, engineering material or appearance mutation.

commands.label: Remove Clear Coat
commands.params: name; target: exact saved definition/feature/component/occurrence_path; expected_revision. Removes only that stable coat assignment in one undo, without device or file access.

commands.label: Save Optical Binding
commands.params: name: CPU or GPU setup; set?: complete numerical setup patch; body_index and body_name: exact captured target; expected_revision; optics:{ior,absorption_per_mm:[r,g,b],boundary:closed_mesh|closed_box|thin_sheet,thickness_mm,shadow_transmission,subsurface?:{scattering_per_mm,anisotropy},model?:{roughness:0..1,dispersion?:{abbe_number:5..200},thin_film?:{ior:1..3,thickness_nm:0..100000}}}; replace?:false. The optional model adds isotropic rough transmission, three-band dispersion and one lossless coherent film. CPU models require explicit Path; rough sheets require straight transmitted shadows off. See docs/render-glass-material-models.md. Stores stable definition/feature/occurrence identity in one undo without modifying engineering geometry/materials. CPU Path consumes at most 128 certified optical targets; the legacy non-Path producer retains eight. Without options.path, sheets and axis-aligned boxes retain the existing transport. Explicit progressive options.path enables exact closed-mesh certification, bounded nested convex-parent media, Beer/Snell/Fresnel and thin transmitted shadows; touching or unproven boundaries and closed transmitted-shadow connections refuse explicitly. Existing subsurface parameters may be consumed on certified closed Path media with denoising explicitly off; scalar free-flight/HG walks and separate Beer absorption are supported without refracting-boundary next-event approximation. A zero scattering rate preserves transport. GPU nested media require separate job.options.nested_media and producer certification. Unresolved or incompatible targets refuse atomically.

commands.label: Remove Optical Binding
commands.params: name: saved setup; target: exact saved definition/feature/component/occurrence_path; expected_revision. Removes only that optical assignment in one undo without a device or file access.

commands.label: Regrade Linear Master
commands.params: job?: exact completed JobId (default selected result); presentation: {exposure_ev?,tone_map?,finishing?,backdrop?,background?,transparent_background?}. Queues cancellable nondestructive PNG presentation from that retained native FLOAT32 master, not from PNG. Captured geometry/camera/lighting and source EXR remain unchanged; no path tracing, denoising, external EXR import or automatic file writes. Returns a distinct job with source identity and original-master digest. Existing frame retention and export rules still apply.

commands.label: Set Render Camera
commands.params: camera: complete Render Camera snapshot (target, yaw, pitch, distance, fov; roll defaults to 0 and up to z). Validates the same finite mm/radian bounds as saved render intent, preserves explicit roll/up and changes only transient view state. No model evaluation, setup save, renderer, dirty flag or undo step. Design view.apply retains its separate up-axis policy.

commands.label: Inspect Render Camera
commands.params: No parameters. Returns the explicitly defined current view camera, or null if the session has no camera override. No camera is fitted, no job is started and no saved setup or engineering document is changed.

commands.label: Frame Render Subject
commands.params: aspect?: the picture's width over its height, 0.000001 to 1000000 (default 1). Fits the current camera to the visible product bounds through the shared Camera::fit contract, moving back for a picture taller than wide so its sides hold the product too; changes only view state, not a saved setup, rendering job, stage or engineering geometry.

commands.label: Review Native Studio
commands.params: id: NATIVE-STUDIO-001..025; name; set?: typed CPU/GPU setup patch; expected_revision?:u64. Resolves original built-in HDR/rig/passive ground with conservative geometry clearance, returns all replacements and preserved fields without mutation. Unbound SCENE-* concepts are not accepted.

commands.label: Apply Native Studio
commands.params: Same reviewed input as render.preset.resolve, expected_revision required, replace_lighting_and_environment:true and replace_stage:true when an existing stage would change. Re-resolves the complete candidate and publishes one undo or no mutation; camera, optical bindings, geometry and engineering materials are preserved.

commands.label: Review Fixed Sampling Budget
commands.params: id: Q-*; variant:fixed_samples_png for the existing GPU projection, or cpu_progressive_png for Q-001/002/003 CPU cost budgets; acknowledge_omissions:true. Optional cpu:{minimum_budget:compact|studio|workstation,adaptive?:captured AdaptiveSampling} selects the smallest existing profile admitting pilots plus production without lowering minimum_budget. CPU budgets use authored sizes, 16/32/64 production samples and seed21026; preserve transport depth, denoise, optics and effects. Read-only numerical projections, not convergence/time guarantees or complete quality acceptance. Never switches executor, adopts fixed CPU sampling or mutates a shot.

commands.label: Duplicate Render Shot
commands.params: name, new_name, expected_revision:u64. Copies exact saved setup and resource references in one undo. Existing destinations refuse; captured jobs and camera navigation are unchanged.

commands.label: Rename Render Shot
commands.params: name, new_name, expected_revision:u64. Renames exact saved setup in one undo; an existing destination or stale review refuses.

commands.label: Remove Render Shot
commands.params: name, expected_revision:u64. Removes only that saved setup in one undo; retains resources, geometry and captured results.

commands.label: Inspect Original Surface Map
commands.params: id: SURF-*. Returns bounded hash-verified original base-color PNG bytes and source-map fidelity label, not a rendered material thumbnail. No external paths, rendering or document edits.

commands.label: Prepare Physical Reference
commands.params: id: named built-in physical profile, name: proposed new material label, acknowledge_reference:true. Read-only loss-aware creation plan using native ValidatedCard admission and one point density; returns source receipts, extended fields and omissions. Does not execute material.create, assign bodies or infer effective-part physics.

commands.label: Save Render Ground
commands.params: name: typed raytrace setup, set?: setup patch, margin_fraction?:0.25, gap_mm?:0.1, reflectance_linear?:[0.18,0.18,0.18], replace_stage?:false. Fits one finite passive ground below the visible product once and saves its physical transforms in one undo. Product AABB separation is rechecked on every render.

commands.label: Save Physical Render Background
commands.params: name: typed raytrace setup, set?: setup patch, kind: floor_wall or cyclorama, reflectance_linear?: [0.18,0.18,0.18], expected_revision: reviewed revision, replace_stage?:false. Fits a finite floor/wall or a 24-strip polygonal cyclorama behind the visible subject using the saved camera azimuth; world +Z up and a minimum one-mm stage envelope. Preserves subject geometry, lighting, output, pose and engineering materials; one undo and rechecked product separation. Not an infinite/analytically smooth/terrain background.

commands.label: Remove Render Stage
commands.params: name: setup, set?: setup patch. Removes saved render-only panels atomically; CAD geometry and lighting are unchanged.

commands.label: Save Surface Binding
commands.params: name: CPU or GPU setup; set?: setup patch; surface: same input as render.library.surface.prepare; replace?: false. Pins exact source hashes and definition/feature/occurrence identity with local-mm mapping in one undo. No paths, mesh ordinals or physical material changes.

commands.label: Remove Surface Binding
commands.params: name: setup, target: saved definition/feature/component/occurrence_path, set?: setup patch. Removes only that explicit binding in one undo; no device or current geometry required.

commands.label: Retain Displayed Render Result
commands.params: job?: completed JobId (default selected result), or null to clear selection. Selects within the eight retained completed results; oldest is evicted first. Preserves exact export bytes and original host memory accounting. No design/undo change; preview or foreign jobs refuse.

commands.label: Find Render Library Targets
commands.params: query?: exact-name substring; offset?:0; limit?:128 (1..128). Returns a bounded page of captured body ordinals/names, revision and scene bounds. Settles the model through ordinary command handling; never returns a large mesh payload.

commands.label: Browse Render Library
commands.params: kind?: surfaces, selene_appearances, hdr, rigs, scenes, materials, lighting, environments, quality, native_scenes, selene_shots or capabilities; query?: bounded search; availability?: all/usable/specification/blocked; offset?:0; limit?:48 (1..128). Returns source status and explicit implemented projections separately. No device, file IO or design change.

commands.label: Inspect Render Library Resource
commands.params: kind, id: exact authored resource. Returns original specification, runtime projection variants and explicit omissions. A concept is not an executable preset.

commands.label: Apply Library Opaque Appearance
commands.params: id: SURF-* or SELENE-AP-*; variant: uniform_opaque (required); bodies: 1..256 exact body names. Applies the original scalar baseline through ordinary appearance assignment in one undo, preserving physical properties. Spatial maps and advanced target effects are explicitly excluded.

commands.label: Apply Built-in HDR Environment
commands.params: id: HDR-*; name: saved setup; set?: typed CPU/GPU setup patch; rotation_rad?: authored rotation (native origin offset is explicit in the reply); intensity?:1; samples?:16 for CPU; replace_environment?:false. Hash-verifies and embeds original bytes, saves one atomic undo without external files or a render device. An HDR-owned sun cannot duplicate an analytic sun.

commands.label: Prepare Authored Surface Maps
commands.params: id: SURF-*; body_index and body_name from render.scene; origin?:[0,0,0]; plane?:xy/yz/zx; scale?:1; rotation_rad?:0 (positive around the plane normal). Returns an explicit GPU temporary planar binding and a source usable by saved CPU/GPU surface.bind, with source hashes, original millimetre scale, image-up normal orientation and absolute base-color semantics. No document change; height/displacement and true anisotropy are not included.

commands.label: Prepare Authored Studio Lights
commands.params: id: RIG-*; variant: complete for emitter-only rigs, emitters_only for rigs with passive cards; center_mm and subject_extent_mm required. Converts exact rectangular half-edges and solar direction/radius. Optional name and typed CPU set return the complete CPU projection and explicit indirect-lighting adoption plan; authored radiance beyond CPU intensity64 refuses without scaling. Blocked calibration and external-sun rigs refuse. Returns a geometry-clearance review requirement; does not create cards or modify the scene.

commands.label: Apply Authored Studio Lights
commands.params: rig: id, variant, center_mm and subject_extent_mm; name; set?: typed CPU/GPU setup patch; expected_revision?:u64; enable_indirect?:false (explicit CPU Sun adoption after review); replace_lighting_and_environment:true required. Saves the explicit rig projection in one undo, removing prior lighting/environment only with that confirmation. Subject clearance still needs review; passive cards are never silently omitted.

commands.label: Inspect HDR Source
commands.params: path: scoped Radiance HDR file; validates the complete bounded source and returns sha256, width, height, encoded_bytes and primaries without saving or rendering

commands.label: Save Render Settings with HDR
commands.params: name, set: typed CPU/GPU setup patch with hdr/environment unset; path: scoped HDR; expected_sha256?: digest returned by render.hdr.inspect (changed sources refuse); rotation_rad?:0, intensity?:1; samples?:1/4/16/64 for CPU only (default16); assume_linear_srgb?:false for GPU only. Captures immutable bytes and saves resource plus setup atomically in one undo, without a host; returns name/setup/resource metadata, never source bytes

commands.label: Check Render Request
commands.params: setup?: saved name OR settings?: full RenderSetup. A typed job selects raster/cpu_raytrace/gpu_path and its numerical options plus embedded HDR before dispatch; only replace and transient studio_weights may accompany it. Without job, the legacy runtime controls below remain available. See docs/render-settings.md. studio_weights?: three finite 0..1 visibility weights for raster or implicit GPU studio sources only; never saved. integrator?: raster (default) or raytrace; progressive?: false (registered GPU path, CPU integrator/LED options are mutually exclusive); texture_filtering?: false (GPU); CPU raytrace.texture_filtering?: false. Explicitly enables ray-footprint mip and bounded anisotropic map filtering on GPU, and bounded anisotropic filtering on CPU. GPU filtering off retains bilinear LOD0; CPU filtering off retains isotropic mip selection, using the coarsest available mip when footprint data is unavailable. samples?: 1..65536; max_depth?: 1..64; seed?: u32 for progressive; raytrace?: bounded runtime progressive/primary_samples/lights/punctual_lights/area_lights/area_samples/seed/exposure_ev/shadows/reflections/anisotropic_faces/emissions/surface_effects/dielectrics/environment options, only with raytrace. CPU raytrace.lens?: {aperture_radius_mm:0..10000000,focus_distance_mm:0.000001..1000000000}; positive aperture requires explicit CPU progressive sampling and a bounded perspective camera; absent/zero keeps the original CPU ray stream. See docs/render-thin-lens.md. CPU raytrace.volume?: one HomogeneousVolume box with world-mm min_mm/max_mm, extinction_per_mm:0..1000, RGB scattering_albedo:0..1 and anisotropy:-0.95..0.95. Positive extinction requires explicit Indirect lighting and cannot combine with Glass/SSS or surface Denoise. Physical eye/pupil prefixes and the orthographic line/box union preserve camera/model framing under existing ray/profile caps. See docs/render-cpu-volume.md. CPU raytrace.sun? uses the shared finite-disk Sun contract; raytrace.sky? uses {gradient,rotation_rad,intensity}. Both require explicit Indirect lighting, and gradient Sky excludes a constant/HDR environment. Their medium NEE uses the HG response/PDF and physical light source; see docs/render-cpu-celestial.md. CPU transparent_background?:false exports straight-alpha primary geometry coverage for fixed/progressive sampling; body/face opacity must remain 1, and active bloom/backdrop/photographic effects require opaque output. CPU raytrace.output?: {tone_map,finishing,backdrop,linear_exr}; shared presentation supports up to 8192 per side and 33554432 output pixels, CPU exposure remains raytrace.exposure_ev; raw FLOAT32 EXR is retained only at final completion. CPU raytrace.budget?: compact (legacy default), studio or workstation; see docs/render-cpu-resource-profiles.md for explicit image/geometry/memory/work limits. CPU raytrace.progressive?: {samples_per_pixel:1..profile limit, seed:u32}; requires primary_samples:1 and selected reflections.samples:1; area/LED sources and certified planar anisotropy/thin-sheet/axis-aligned-box dielectric continuations share the existing bounded transport and compatibility checks. See docs/render-cpu-progressive.md; environment?: {path: scoped HDR, expected_sha256?: inspected digest, rotation_radians: 0, intensity: 1, samples: 16} OR {resource: saved HDR digest, rotation_radians, intensity, samples}; embedded resources cannot combine with path/hash; explicit sRGB/D65 HDR primaries required. Opaque CPU preview with selected mirror/rough-specular reflections and certified planar anisotropy. HDR with rough reflections or anisotropy requires fully metallic selected bodies and all effective faces; unsupported combinations refuse. Optional raytrace.path:{max_depth:1..64} enables CPU diffuse/specular GI with matched rectangle/HDR light and BSDF MIS plus certified closed-mesh Glass. It requires explicit progressive camera sampling, primary_samples:1 and traced shadows; selected reflections and certified anisotropy refuse before HDR IO without changing intent. CPU Path dielectric subsurface?:{scattering_per_mm:0..100,anisotropy:-0.95..0.95} enables homogeneous free-flight/HG walks inside certified closed media; positive rates require denoising off. Contained light connections include scattering survival; closed refractive light connections and combining Glass with external volume remain unsupported. Absent path keeps the old certified thin_sheet/closed_box producer and refuses subsurface intent explicitly. See docs/render-cpu-general-glass.md and render-raytrace-dielectrics.md. CPU emissions are visible radiance and may light neighbors through sampled Path continuation, without mesh-emitter next-event sampling; surface_effects change roughness/shading normals without geometry changes. led_strip?: continuous world-mm LED rectangle recipe; led_samples?: 1/4/16/64 for the whole strip, default16. At most8directional+8punctual+4rectangle/LED sources; shared area N. See docs/render-light-union.md. transparent_background?: false; replace?: false. With progressive:true, raytrace instead accepts GPU dielectrics/clear_coats/textures; environment instead accepts tagged hdr/embedded_hdr/sky with rotation_rad/intensity; file hdr supports expected_sha256, embedded_hdr uses a document resource digest. See docs/render-hdr-resources.md. GPU lens, studio lighting, tone_map, denoise, clamp_indirect?: 0.000001..1000000 (biased; caps each contribution from the first bounce on, keeping its hue; see docs/render-path.md), bounded finishing/backdrop and linear_exr retention are also available. CPU raytrace and GPU top-level controls accept supersampling:1|2 (default 1; doubles internal width and height at 2, averages scene-linear premultiplied samples before tone mapping, exports selected dimensions), denoise_settings:{passes:1..3,strength:0..1,firefly_suppression:bool,optical_filter:bool}, and denoise_diagnostics:false. Optical filtering defaults to true for eligible mirror/glass guides; optical_filter:false restores legacy opaque-only display denoising. Guides and diagnostics retain their independent eligibility policy and conservative highlight protection. CPU raytrace.threads:0..64 selects bounded automatic workers at 0 (default), serial work at 1 or an explicit count from 2 through 64. Resource checks include internal image buffers and worker scratch. See docs/render-quality-controls.md. Both path tracers accept optional metal_energy_compensation: true for rough isotropic metals (inside CPU raytrace or top-level GPU). Both methods accept optional caustics {photons:1..1048576,radius_mm:0.000001..1000000,max_depth:1..64,seed:u32,area_lights?:false,environment?:false,guided_emission?:false,refresh_per_pass?:false} (inside CPU raytrace; top-level GPU). Optical assignments accept optional model {roughness:0..1,dispersion?:{abbe_number:5..200},thin_film?:{ior:1..3,thickness_nm:0..100000}}. CPU advanced models require Path; rough sheets require straight transmitted shadows off. See docs/render-glass-material-models.md. GPU adaptive?: {pilot_samples:16..256,min_samples:16..samples,relative_error:0..1,absolute_error:0.000001..1000000,coverage_error:0.001..0.25} allocates independent production budgets; pilots are discarded, not a certified error guarantee. transmission_samples?:1|2|4 stratifies the first Fresnel branch with extra path cost. volume?:{min_mm:[x,y,z],max_mm:[x,y,z],extinction_per_mm:0..1000,scattering_albedo:[r,g,b],anisotropy:-0.95..0.95} is one finite homogeneous world-mm medium; active media require explicit lighting/environment and refuse glass, denoise and multiple transmission strata. These fields also persist in GPU job.options. See docs/render-materials/TRANSPORT-MASTER-BATCH-2026-10-23.md; see docs/render-transmission.md, render-environment.md, render-runtime-textures.md, render-thin-lens.md, render-studio-lighting.md and render-denoise.md. Optional CPU raytracing requires a raytrace-cpu build and native host, checked before scene capture. Stale geometry is rejected. See docs/render-jobs.md

commands.label: Render Image
commands.params: Same request as render.preflight. Captures an immutable product scene and queues a bounded image job. Returns its session-scoped job identity, captured scene_generation and progress. Does not change the design. See docs/render-jobs.md

commands.label: Render Progress
commands.params: job?: {session, serial, generation}. Non-blocking progress, errors and captured frame metadata with queue:{running,waiting,job,shot,error}. Without job returns queue only. Advances an explicitly started render.batch through render.start as jobs finish; never pumps render work. Preview is separate from the exportable final image.

commands.label: Cancel Render
commands.params: job?: {session, serial, generation}, default the active render.batch job. Requests cooperative cancellation and drops its waiting shots; completed jobs remain completed. Late cancelled frames cannot be published.

commands.label: Copy Render Image
commands.params: job?: completed JobId (default selected result). Validates the retained PNG for app clipboard copying (max 4096 per side, 4194304 pixels); headless returns frame metadata only. Never copies a provisional image or starts a job.

commands.label: Export Render Image
commands.params: job?: {session, serial, generation} (default selected result), path: destination matching format?: png (default), exr or denoise_mask (PNG extension), overwrite?: false. Guide masks require denoise_diagnostics captured during rendering; their separate bytes, dimensions and SHA are returned under denoise_mask, while frame identifies the parent colour result. EXR requires an opt-in raw linear master retained by that completed CPU or GPU job; never converts PNG pixels. Exports a retained completed image atomically; an existing destination is preserved on failure. See docs/render-jobs.md

commands.label: Render Backends
commands.params: No parameters. Returns {schema_version: 1, default_backend: builtin, backends: [{id, label, availability, executors: [{id, availability, profiles, limits, scratch}]}]}. Metadata only; does not start rendering or probe a GPU. See docs/render-backends.md

commands.label: Render Settings
commands.params: name?: saved setup. Without name returns {setups, defaults}; with name returns {name, setup}. Does not evaluate the model or apply a camera. See docs/render-settings.md

commands.label: Save Render Settings
commands.params: name: setup name, set: object of fields to replace (backend, mode, camera, width, height, format, exposure_ev, environment_rotation, environment_intensity, background, job, surfaces, optics, coats, stage). job?: typed active raster/cpu_raytrace/gpu_path configuration with optional validated embedded HDR reference; omitted preserves, null clears, object replaces the complete job. Creates from defaults and saves without a host, validates atomically, one undo step; identical edits are no-ops. See docs/render-settings.md

commands.label: Inspect Render Scene
commands.params: No parameters. Authoritative product-scene metadata, without modelling overlays or mesh payloads. Explicitly settles stale geometry; does not render an image. See docs/render-workspace.md

commands.label: Apply Render Camera
commands.params: name: saved setup. Applies its existing Camera snapshot including roll/up as view state, without modifying the document or starting a render.

commands.label: Copy Render Check Report
commands.params: text: nonempty report, at most 65536 bytes. Validated clipboard request; headless echo only, never renders or edits a design.

commands.label: Select Render Result
commands.params: index: integer 0..7, oldest first; must be retained. Selects a completed result as transient per-document view state; echoes index.

commands.label: Discard Render Result
commands.params: index: integer 0..7, oldest first; must be retained. Drops only that transient result, selecting the newest remaining result if necessary; echoes index.

commands.label: Set Render Output Size
commands.params: width, height: 1..16384; custom?: bool. Validated Render output draft request; headless echo only, no design edits or job. The UI separately limits new selections to 8192 per side, 33554432 output pixels and the selected rendering profile.

commands.label: View Render Image
commands.params: view: model|image|fit|actual|denoise_mask. Guide-mask view requires a selected completed result captured with denoising diagnostics. Validated result canvas request; headless echo only, never starts a job.

commands.label: Close Render Image
commands.params: No parameters. Return to Model Preview; headless echo only, never cancels a job.

commands.label: Paint Appearance
commands.params: appearance or color/name/opacity/pbr: appearance.assign look parameters; validates and returns look for ui.start paint. done?: true ends the UI tool. Programmatic calls never open UI.

commands.label: Pick Up Appearance
commands.params: target?: appearance.chain target; returns its resolved look, or requests the UI sampling tool when omitted. Programmatic calls never open UI.

commands.label: Solo Light
commands.params: id?: kind:slot light address; solo:bool. Enabling requires an id; false clears solo. Validates and echoes per-document UI view state. Never saves settings, evaluates geometry, opens an editor or changes history.

commands.label: Mute Light
commands.params: id: kind:slot light address; mute:bool. Validates and echoes per-document UI view state, applied to live preview and captured render copies only. Never changes saved settings or history.

commands.label: Compare Images
commands.params: left, right: live or retained result index 0..7 (oldest first), distinct and retained; OR off:true. Validated per-document comparison view request; headless echo, no rendering or design/history change.

commands.label: Move Render Comparison Divider
commands.params: position: finite number, clamped to 0.05..0.95. Transient comparison divider request; headless echo only.

commands.label: Render All Shots
commands.params: request?: render.start parameters, shared across all saved shots except camera. Default: first saved setup in name order. Captures up to 32 shot cameras and queues sequentially through render.start; returns {queued:n}. Refuses active renders, no shots or stale geometry. render.status (also with {}) and the UI tick advance the queue; Cancel on the active job drops waiting shots. No design/history/revision change.
